sources.oracle_body:
Kicker {2}{W}{W}
Choose target creature you own. If this spell was kicked, instead choose any number of target creatures you own. Return each chosen creature to your hand. At the beginning of the next upkeep, create a 4/4 white Bird Soldier creature token with flying for each creature returned to your hand this way.
sources.rules: Cached official Comprehensive Rules 2026-09-25: 111.8 token departure/cease timing; 400.7 exact new zone object; 603.7a/b/d creation, next event once, source and controller; 608.2b legality; 608.2h information sampling; kicker 702.33.
source_discrepancies: Java schedules target-pointer list size; Oracle requires actual successful returns. Rust counts frozen actual moved-to-Hand events.
Pinned BirdSoldier44Token omits Soldier subtype; exact Oracle Bird Soldier recipe takes precedence.

shared_mechanics: Private ReturnTargetsCreateNextUpkeep batches all surviving legal exact targets through move_objects_raw, freezes actual successful hand-return count, registers one owned delayed SpellView, then finishes zone events. Linked-return entry suspension cannot lose or replay the count.

Sparse optional delayed-upkeep registry participates in clone/snapshot/rollback and owned-byte accounting. It transfers once into normal pending triggers at the next actual upkeep of any player. Independent original spells retain separate rows.

Private ResolveDelayedTokenCreation passes the frozen amount and original resolving controller to existing replacement-aware create_tokens. Spell source departure and later returned-card changes do not affect the obligation.

Existing ownership predicate, kicker target adjustment, targeting legality, cost payment, generic countering, APNAP preparation, token SBA and replacement/entry continuations are reused. No activation-payment or mana-funding behavior changed; funding/targeting exhaustive StackKind classifications gain the new kind.

assertion_map.obligation: Both seats pay printed 1W during opposing combat; owned foreign-controlled creature qualifies, controlled foreign-owned creature is rejected. Successful hand return schedules no immediate token; any-player next upkeep makes one untapped white 4/4 Bird Soldier with flying owned by resolving spell controller. Later upkeep does not repeat.
Both seats actually pay printed cost plus 2WW kicker, choose zero targets, and resolve. One zero-amount delayed trigger still occurs next upkeep and creates no tokens.

Both seats pay kicker and select multiple owned creatures including an opposing-controlled creature and a token. All successful hand moves count before the token ceases to exist; later hand-to-graveyard/battlefield changes do not change the frozen count.
One stale exact incarnation is ignored while surviving legal targets return; all stale targets fizzle the spell without scheduling. A target that becomes noncreature before resolution is excluded.

Resolving during an already-begun upkeep waits for the following upkeep. Independent spells schedule distinct delayed triggers. Countering one trigger leaves the other intact and creates only its frozen token amount.

Creation replacements are sampled at actual delayed resolution. Two Doubling Seasons added after scheduling multiply one token to four. Suspended replacement choice supports owned raw/index branches, parent drop, snapshot restore and exactly-once continuation.

An actual Banishing Light exile is followed by typed creature animation and paid kicked return of it plus another creature. Both hand moves and frozen count commit before the linked Adaptive Automaton entry choice suspends. Owned raw/index, parent drop and restore resume once and preserve the two-token result.
An actual paid Negate counters the spell, leaving its target in play with no delayed row. Insufficient kicker payment is rejected transactionally without a hand move or delayed state.

A late next-stack-id capacity failure after attempted movement rolls back the complete action: target zone/generation, snapshot, revision and both player observations remain unchanged, with no delayed row.
